utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-04-75-T, The Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Lisa Biersay, on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor, along with STA Douglas Stringer, Case Manager, Thomas Laugel, and our legal intern, Marina Marcikic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, Zoran Zivanovic and Christopher Gosnell. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The witness may be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Celar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- Mrs. Celar. I'd like to begin today by asking you whether you recognise some names whom the Prosecution believes there's evidence showing that they were active in Beli Manastir. You already describe knowing Borivoje Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Is that correct? And he was the president of the Beli Manastir Executive Council --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know him as that, I knew him as mayor.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You knew him as mayor?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know someone by the name of Lazar Bronovic?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And the information we have is that he is -- he was the head of the TO in Beli Manastir in 1991. You didn't --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the TO is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of that term?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Was he?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of that name.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What about Bovoje Dobrokes?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard of that name. I didn't know him but I know that Dobrokes or similar.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Dobrokes is that a familiar name?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something similar to that but I didn't think was the ... I thought it ended in a -- there was a "s" in there somewhere, but I could say it's a similar name to a name that I was aware of.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know who the head of the Baranja TO was?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What about Svetislav Branic?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard of that name as well, Branic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you know him as a commander of the local police?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know them. I just heard of names, but never went anywhere near them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What about the name Milan Jaric?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jaric, I knew him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what did you know him as?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the -- the same groups as my husband was in. They were fighting on the front lines. And later, I knew that his son had been killed in a motorcycle accident. So that's how I knew him, the two reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Have you heard the name Milos Mamula?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And in your -- this is a place not a person in your statement, I believe it's paragraph 48, you mention a place called Devil's Bridge?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I don't have a copy of my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Well, I believe it has been admitted now as D173, if I'm correct. So --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could just see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Sure, please.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about Devil's Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is somewhere between Osijek and -- I don't know the specific location. On the front line between Osijek and ... well, I would say Beli Manastir, but I actually mean that part of Baranja that was controlled by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I've never been there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: But you heard about it?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told about it by my husband and by some of the wives.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did Ilija Celar or anyone else tell you that before the conflict began, Serbs were only 25.5 per cent of the Beli Manastir municipality population?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that figure. I remember seeing - I can't say it was Ilija that showed me, it could have been - a breakdown of the population, the census, but there was a lot of argument about the census as being people who had put their names down as Yugoslavian were classified as Croatian. That's was the claim of it but I don't know the veracity of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Just to be clear, Ilija Celar showed you the 1991 census?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say it was him. I saw it -- I saw it -- but I don't recall if he -- he could have showed to me but it's not something I remember, but I remember seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When did you see it?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you. I don't know. I didn't even know it was around that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you -- was it before 1992 or after?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Were you also aware that the Hungarian population was about 16.5 per cent before --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- the census.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall these figures.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm asking you that because in paragraph 81 of your statement in the last sentence, you say: "There were many Hungarians living in Baranja at that time and I am to the totally unaware of any of them leaving."

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, because we used to go to the villages. They -- some of the villages sold very good wine, and I'd visited some of those villages. I went to one of the -- I can't remember the name of it -- one of the Hungarian villages where the family of my girlfriend lived because they'd got a goat, a small goat that had been orphaned and they asked me if I'd take it because they knew I liked animals. So I went to this Hungarian village to take the goat, with her, she drove me there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Is that your basis for concluding that you're unaware of any of the Hungarians leaving?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just because I didn't hear anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So Ilija Celar didn't tell you --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- about that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So are you saying you know for a fact that not one of the 16.5 per cent of the Hungarian population left?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know it as a fact. And because people were coming and going all the time, I have to say that the names, if somebody left, it wasn't expressed as an ethnic person that had left. It was expressed as a name. So-and-so has left from wherever they'd left.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So you could have heard the names of people leaving but you wouldn't necessarily associate an ethnicity with them. Is that what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't the key issue. You could assume. I couldn't tell the difference then between Serbian names and Croatian names.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you could usually understand a Hungarian name.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd-like to take a quick look at Exhibit 3039 which is tab 68. Now, you can see this is a letter dated October 18, 1991, and it's for the minister for foreign affairs, the Republic of Hungary.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you see it says: "From various reliable sources, the following information has reached us about developments ..." And on the next page, discusses the forcible changes in the ethnic composition of the population on the territories ... most openly in the Baranja region. The replacement of 6300 expelled Hungarians and even more Croats by 13.000 Serbs is under way." Did you know about 6300 expelled Hungarians?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now this was happening sometime before October 18, 1991, so you actually were not --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You weren't there then?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And this is not something that Ilija Celar told you about; right?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: There's some other documents in this regard, but I'd like to hold off on them and move on to another topic and I may come back to it. What I'd like to ask you about now is paragraph 80 of your statement where you said: "I believe the first time I saw the Red Berets was 1994."

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Why did you think that the people you were seeing were, in fact, Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were wearing red berets. I'd never seen anybody wearing red berets in Beli Manastir before.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And that was in 1994?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I ask you this because I'd like to show you - let me just make sure I have the right tab number - it would be Exhibit 2852, tab 60. And if we could go to page 3 of that. And this is a document dated 2 June 1992. And it's a report from UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It will come on your screen --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- hopefully in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So P2852, tab 60. And I want to go to item 8 on that page that starts with: "From BelBat ..." Let me check the -- is there an issue with the -- the number that I can help with? So page 3. And if we could expand 8 from BelBat. And I'll read it for the record: "The Red Berets, special antiterrorist police, have not left Baranja. They are now in blue uniforms, milicija. Several persons have surely been identified by UN personal," which I think is meant to be personnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So according to this, the Red Berets had, in fact, were now dressed differently --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what year we're talking about? I'm not clear about this at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: This one is 1992 so I just --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. This is 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Correct. That in 1992 already, the uniforms of the Red Berets had changed?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd never seen any Red Berets before the -- 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we could now go, I believe, to Exhibit 2863, which is tab 63 - I'll check, yes. And now going to page 4. At the very top where it says "Sector East," can you read that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And it says: "In Baranja, Red Berets have disappeared. Some of them have been recognised in regular police clothing and in civilian clothing, having a milicija ID card." So what I am putting to you is with the arrival of UNPROFOR, the Red Berets began changing their uniforms in order to blend in with the police and they were, in fact, not wearing red berets.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't recall exactly when they did it, but they took all the uniforms off. My husband certainly stopped wearing a uniform when the -- when the deployment started, within -- I can't be exact, the date, I don't remember. But within a short time of, I thought, of the deployment, all the men stopped wearing uniforms. And when I saw the Red Berets in 1994, they were the only ones wearing uniforms. Nobody else -- they were all in civilian clothes. I would know more exactly if I could remember exactly when my husband started working for BelBat -- not Belbat, CIVPOL.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when you say deployment, do you mean the UNPROFOR deployment?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think I mean CIVPOL, when they came. By that time, all the uniforms were gone, and -- but these Red Berets came back and did -- really terrorised everybody, didn't matter who you were, any nationality at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you see here that UNPROFOR is talking about the Red Berets in Baranja in 1992 where --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I -- I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You didn't see them then. Why did you your husband stop wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they were all told they had to disarm and hand in all their uniforms, which they did. But I don't know what date that was. But all the guns and everything they'd got was handed in. And uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You realise that UNPROFOR's position was, in fact, they did not disarm even though they changed uniforms.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about the Red Berets? I'm not talking about them, I'm talking about my husband.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I am talking about the other forces that were in Baranja at this time.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only talk about my husband and the people I knew that were his friends, because he then got his job working for BelBat.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Hold was Ilija Celar in 1991?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was born in 1956.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So he was definitely of mobilisation age?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And he, in fact, was mobilised?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether he was mobilised. I don't -- they -- no, they were never officially mobilised as far as I knew. They'd got a -- formed a defence group, 19 private citizens met together, and that's how it started.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did his unit have a name what he was part of?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. No, they weren't -- after the fighting - if I could just give you an indication of what I thought the position was. After the -- there were 46 of them involved in the fighting from the 19th of August to the 23rd, about then.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: 23rd of --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1991, August.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And this is information that you got from Ilija Celar --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- because you weren't there?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- he told me. And he also told me that the Yugoslav Army were there but they were watching them. And in fact, when my husband went up the rain tower where the flour is stored in Beli Manastir and they put the flag up there, the Serbian flag. And we they came back down again, they were arrested by the army who asked them what they were doing. So it wasn't -- he wasn't mobilised, let me put that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: But he wore a uniform?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what uniform did he wear?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, initially they had a blue, like a police uniform. And then when they had -- when they start going to the front line, there, then they all changed in the camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now you describe in your statement that he returned from the front lines. I believe this is in paragraph 32: "That on the 23rd or 24 of August, 1991, he was called back from the front line with Boro Zivanovic."

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me about this. I have no personal knowledge of it. We were talking about journalists, how many journalists had been in Baranja.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So Ilija Celar participated in the take-over of Beli Manastir, right, there's no -- you've already --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Okay. And he was the one who told you about it and he's the one who gave you all the information for paragraphs 26, 31, 32 --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. 26, some of it came from my neighbour about what had been happening. Some of it came from friends that I met afterwards. But the information about the people that were killed came from Ilija.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And the information about the JNA, what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, came from Ilija.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Okay. Did Ilija Celar tell you about non-Serbs being killed, beaten, tortured during the period of time that you were away?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because most of the time he was on the front line, but later he did when I came back, because he'd been instrumental in intervening - I was very proud of him - in stopping or releasing people that had been taken into custody without any real reason at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met some of them afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So Croats were being taken in for no reason or Serbs as well?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said that. He saw that the people that had been taken in without good reason, as he saw it, he would intervene.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what ethnicity were these people?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one I met, I'm not sure whether he was Hungarian or Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know this person's name?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it with me. I do know it but not -- I didn't put the notes. I went and met him at his home because he didn't leave Baranja, he stayed. And the other one was a priest from Djakova. Ilija knew the family. He was Croatian. They said he was a -- had as a sympathiser.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And did he?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ilija went and took him out of the police station. It was chaotic then.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did he --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: And took him to the border.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: He took him to the border?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Took him to the border gave him enough dinars, Hungarian border, so he could get back to -- Ilija did that for him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So he could get back to where?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Djakova. He wanted to go to his seminary. He said he continue his studies in the Djakova seminary.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did Ilija Celar describe non-Serbs being killed, beaten and tortured not just about the people he saved but of this happening to -- to non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not about killings. He said that they were being beaten up in the police station, which enraged him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And who was doing the beating up?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know because -- this is the very early 1991 and they were mainly on the front line. So when he came back from the front line, it was chaos in the -- people were putting uniforms on. They weren't real police there. Those that didn't want to fight, I think, and go to the front line went to become policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I can't tell you. I'm now speculating because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Because you weren't there.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And the information you got --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did Ilija Celar ever express the idea that Serbs, Serb fighters, had their own truth?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know what that means.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you ever hear him say that the Baranja area was Serb holy land?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, you describe around at the end of August that Ilija Celar was called back from the front lines in order to meet with foreign journalists.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not meet them, to be an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: To be an interpreter. Thank you. I'd like to now turn to 65 ter number 6572, which, I believe, is tab 91.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And directing my attention now to the Trial Chamber -- just to inform the Chamber, that this is something that we -- we found after our 65 ter exhibit list was finalized, and it is not currently part of the 65 ter exhibit list for the Prosecution. So we would move for its addition. And I'd like to discuss it with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't think the document needs to be on the Prosecution's 65 ter list to be discussed with the document -- or discussed with the witness, so I would suggest that the document is used and admissibility is discussed at a later time. But certainly admission to the Prosecution 65 ter list is neither here nor there, I would suggest.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm happy to proceed in the manner by -- dictated by the Trial Chamber. I would like to show Mrs. Celar the exact words instead of merely quoting them to her, and I believe the direction from the Trial Chamber was that in order to show something to the witness, it had to be on the 65 ter exhibit list. Given that we're now in the Defence phase and reacting to their witness that we've just been given notice of -- not just, but certainly after the finalization of our 65 ter exhibit list, we would like to be able to use additional documents with witnesses, and this is one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just to be clear, Mr. President. There's no objection to using the document if it's not on the 65 ter exhibit list. That's our understanding that it can be used without being on that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And afterwards, eventually, Ms. Biersay, you would tender the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour. You understand me well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: At that -- at that moment, we can admit it to the 65 ter list and admit it as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I see. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So you may proceed and show the document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So if we can now go to 65 ter exhibit number 6572, this is an article that's dated September 3, 1991, which is around the time that you describe Mr. Celar assisting Mayor Zivanovic with interpretation with foreign journalists.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I presume so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You presume so. In your statement, you said that --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is that document, I meant, excuse me. I can't see it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Let me see if I can assist. For now it's just the date. It is entitled: Croatian corn belt becomes a bargaining chip," and the date is on the next line, September 3, 1991. Do you see the date?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you describe that Ilija Celar was called back from the front lines sometime between the 23rd and 24th of August, 1991 to assist with foreign journalists.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: That's what he told you. Now, I'd like to direct your attention, if we could down a few more lines, and there is a sentence that begins: "Reporters trying to travel in the region ..." Do you see that --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: "Reporters trying to travel in the region have been stopped and questioned. One Croatian reporter is missing. One group of photographers came under fire and abandoned their car in the zone on Sunday. 'This is our holy land. You cannot understand this. We're not interested in western opinion or what the world thinks of us,' Ilija Celar told a small group of the first western reporters to reach the capital since its siege. 'We have our truth.'"

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And it also goes on to describe Celar as one of the Serbian irregulars holding the region, saying that he: "... declined to describe what had happened in the area." So Mr. Celar was, in fact, one of the -- the Serb -- a member of the Serb forces who facilitated the take-over [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said there were 19 of them to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And so did Ilija Celar express to you that this, indeed was -- that Baranja was holy land -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... no, he didn't. I'd like to say that this is written by a Croatian journalist and I've read other things written by Croatian journalists, and as such, that's how I regard it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you mean that because it is a Croatian journalist it is --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Biased.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- biased?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could you please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So are you saying that all articles by Croatian journalists are biased?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Some of them are --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you regard this one as being biased.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Truthfully, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's the way it's written. It says that Ilija declined to describe what had happened in the area. I don't -- he may not have been in that area. Which area are they precisely talking about? I haven't understood that from this -- he was Beli Manastir, and then they moved towards Osijek. At some point, the Croatian police went through with safe passage to Osijek. But I don't know what this reference is about why he declined to describe what had happened in the area, where they talk shattered windows and machine-gun fire. It's a motive, and it's inferring that he is hiding something. That's why I think this is biased; it's not factual.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You don't think that Ilija Celar would try to hide anything?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In your -- in your statement, Mrs. Celar, you describe that while you were away in the UK, that Ilija Celar frequently called you from the police station at Beli Manastir to give you updates.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's where I think it was because there weren't any other phones available at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And how regularly would Ilija Celar go to the police station in Beli Manastir?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't -- it was so I wouldn't worry that he wasn't safe. So I don't actually remember. Could have been days apart. Wasn't weeks apart. But it was days apart. But I can't remember now specifically to answer that question. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So is it fair to say you don't know how often he was going to the police station in general, not just to call you, but in general?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Because you weren't there?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you -- did Ilija Celar tell you that in 1991 the Red Berets frequented that police station?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He may have done, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: How far is Bilje --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bilje.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Bilje from Osijek?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's the very first place that you come to after you've crossed the bridge, the first village into Baranja before Darda.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And Ilija Celar also participated in the take-over of Bilje; right?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was on the road to Osijek, to the bridge. There was only that one bridge to get out of Baranja into Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: But he participated in that [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he would have done, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And that was, according to the information I have, in September 1991?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know now how long it continued.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you hear about the Serb forces capturing the radio-television transmitter in Baranja?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Excuse me, I may have done, but it's not something I remember now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I understand. I won't show you this video, which is P2155. I would like to read a bit from it, the transcript, which is -- there should be in e-court. And I believe it's tab 28. And it references Goran Hadzic. And, in this, he was asked about the transmitter at Bilje. He was asked about returning it. And he said --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, could we have a page reference, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It would be page 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: He said: "It is absurd that you're asking -- that they are asking you to return it. Baranja has been liberated. Ustashas have been expelled on Baranja territory of the people who remained there." All of -- it -- sorry. "It means Serbs, Hungarians and Slavonians who didn't do anything wrong. Our units took over the transmitter, they liberated it, and it's normal for us to decide which programme to broadcast." But you didn't hear about the take-over of this transmitter?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wouldn't really have been any interest to me. I mean, I didn't -- I wouldn't have regarded it as relevant to me. And thought about it at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Celar. Mrs. Celar, Mr. Gosnell has tried to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It's just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just a moment Mr. Gosnell. Mr. Gosnell tried to intervene between the question and the answer but he didn't have the chance because you -- you were overlapping again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So please keep in mind -- and there is a very simple trick to do this. Look at the screen. I suppose you have the screen with the transcript before you where you see everything that is said being noted. When the cursor stops, the recorder has finished -- the interpreters have finished, and then you can start your answer. Then you will be in nobody's way. Thank you. Mr. Gosnell, do you still want to intervene?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you know that Ilija Celar had been ordered to find this radio equipment?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You had a friend at the Politika paper; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't a friend. He was a journalist.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not before he rang me in Britain.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So I'd like to now turn your attention to Exhibit 3221.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is that P3221?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes, P3221. Which is tab 75. And if we could zoom in to around the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And two things: You note the first -- the quote begins: "The government has full control over the territorial of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And this article is dated 29 August 1991. Do you also see in the middle of that paragraph where it's attributed to Goran Hadzic: "We will invite all the Serbs outside Serbian countries, the Serbs from Zagreb, Rijeka and other parts of the current Croatia who do not wish to stay in the Ustasha state, to come to Baranja, as Baranja is Serbian. There are empty houses here, which the Ustashas moved into after 1941, and they will not be coming back." Do you see that attributed to him?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And, in fact, there were empty houses in Baranja at that time.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Emptied by non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbs and non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Serbs and non-Serbs. I'd like to turn your attention to the second page of this exhibit where it says: "Radio Beli Manastir equipment returned." And it's dated 28 August. In particular, I want to move to the second indentation. It's an incomplete paragraph, the one -- the one that reads: "We were issued..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: "We were issued an order to find and return the radio equipment." We were told by a participant in the operation, Ilija Celar. "We conducted about 50 raids until we found the equipment ..." And that continues on the next page.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, it said ten raids.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Excuse me, yes, ten raids. "We conducted around ten raids until we found the equipment," and that is attributed to Ilija Celar.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to duty that, in fact, he was given an order and conducted those raids to finds the radio equipment?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't doubt that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And is that because it is coming from Politika?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's because there were only about 40-something fighters at that time. So it would have been probably him or someone else I knew in that situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to paragraph -- let me make sure I have the right number. Paragraph 46 of your statement. And there you describe Ilija Celar being arrested. You say in your statement that it was at the behest of Rade Kostic.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: There was no question.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: My question is: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Who told you that? I just want a name, please.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been the judge I went to see, or it could -- the local judge whose name was, um ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Did Ilija Celar tell you that it was because of Rade Kostic?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They wouldn't let me see him because we weren't married at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: But later, did he ever tell you why he was arrested and imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them. There were 16 of them. He wasn't alone. The whole group had been arrested.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Again, my question is: Did Ilija Celar ever tell you, confirm to that you it was Rade Kostic?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes he thought it was part of a conspiracy.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Part of a conspiracy.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what exactly was the allegation against him?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he and others had murdered a Serbian man in one of the villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when did this happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. The question is vague.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If the witness is able to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What is "this" referring to, Mr. President. That should be specified for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If I may say, that the witness said that allegation was he and others had murdered a Serbian man in one of the villages. And my question is when did this happen. So she's identified an event and I'm asking about the time that relates to it. And I find it very interesting that Mr. Gosnell would get up at this juncture, I must say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, Mr. President, I don't appreciate the imputation. It was a run-of-the-mill intervention requesting for clarification so the witness would clearly understand that the word "this" is referring to the event that is the subject of the allegation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If that was an objection, Mr. Gosnell, the objection is overruled. Please proceed, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When did this alleged murder of a Serbian man happen?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't actually know because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you -- your -- your statement describes it for several paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came back as -- in response to a message I had from Ilija, from the prison somebody got a message out.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you. My question to you is: During the time you're getting information from Ilija Celar for paragraphs 46, 47, 48, did he ever tell you when this alleged murder happened?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did know but I don't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'll help you. And the reason I'm asking, Mrs. Celar, is because, do you know that your -- you do know that your husband was charged for a crime, a murder; correct?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you used your connections with the Serbian lobby to have him released.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't immediate, and it was as a result of the evidence that was brought forward that all those there at that time, in that area, were taken by the police and had all their hands checked for gun powder residue.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So when you say that "I called my contacts with the Serbian lobby in London and complained about this --"

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Being the arrest, "... threatened I wouldn't help them anymore until pressure was brought to bear to get the group out of jail.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So you used your contacts with the Serbian lobby to have him released.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a very good reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: For a very good reason, okay.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I answer that?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I will get do it, Madam Celar. The information we have is that murder occurred on 31st of December, 1991, and that would coincide with the time that you got the information about him being in prison in January of 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I would think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And the information we have is this also happened in Ceminac, which is the place you described you and your husband spending time.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that it was Ceminac. I don't remember where it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What I'd like to do now is to move to tab 97, I believe. And I'll tell you, Mrs. Celar, we requested documents pertaining to your husband from the Republic of Croatia, and we were delivered, night before last, with 200 pages pertaining to your husband. Now some of this we've managed to very quickly translate, and I'd like to ask you about the information contained in that documentation that we received, and documentation we haven't before seen regarding your husband. So if we could move to -- if we could move to 65 ter 6603. And according to this document -- this is a judgement. And if we go to the second page, at the very top of the page, you see Ilija Celar's name --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And this document finds guilty Dario Cvetkovic, Ilija Celar, Savo Jokovic, Dragan Kovacevic, found them all guilty of killing a man by the name of Stevo Pulic. On the third page, it shows that Ilija Celar was, in fact, convicted in absentia and sentenced to ten years in prison. Did you know this?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 2006, my husband was found not guilty of all charges in the Croatian court in Osijek because I'd contacted the -- so this is how I knew about it. In 2006. All charges were given as unfounded and I contacted Interpol and asked them to remove his name from the lists, and they did. Because they said they had no outstanding charges against my husband.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you say that happened in --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In 2006. And who did you contact about that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got -- we had a lawyer in Osijek, who went to Osijek. The court judgement was only displayed outside the court in Osijek and we didn't find out about that judgement until 2011. Then we appointed a lawyer to find out what had happened. He provided us with the judgement that all charges against Ilija Celar had been dropped --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you have a copy of that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But it's easy to get.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Have you -- have you provided a copy of that to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't ask me for it. And then I wrote to Interpol in France asking for his name to be removed from the red notices which they replied they would since there was no outstanding warrants or, et cetera, against him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And do you have that documentation?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He has that at home.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, this document, according to this document, there was an appeal judgement that was also confirmed later in 2002. And you are saying that in 2006 --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- the charges were completely dropped?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, and the charges then were -- there were no -- they stated there were no outstanding charges against Ilija because he was also charged with rebellion against -- or something like rebellion against the state of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Are you talking about the rebellion charge being dropped?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, all charges.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Or just the murder was dropped?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They dismissed all -- they said no charges outstanding in his case, the court of Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So I'd like to show you another document. And this is at -- well, first let me ask you this: Are you aware that in March of 2001, Croatia initiated an international search for Ilija Celar for the murder he's alleged to have committed against detainees in Beli Manastir --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... we weren't aware of that until I saw it on the Internet.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When did you see that on the Internet?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about 2009. I can't be specific. I wasn't looking for anything like that. It could have been somebody told us about it. But there was something like 50 people being charged.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And why were you looking for that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I think somebody had told me about it. That there were about 50 people -- no, I know why. Someone contacted Ilija and said that he was one of the ones that were being charged with crimes by -- I don't know which crimes, by Croatia. And it was actually one of these people that was talking to Ilija. Then I went and found it on the Internet and then they talked about getting a lawyer. And then that's how Ilija found that in 2006, they had been found not guilty of any charges -- that Croatia had no outstanding charges against them, and they were free of all prosecution. They named 16 out of the 50 and Ilija was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And that was for the murder of Stevo Pulic, the Serb --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was all charges but were no outstanding charges against Ilija Celar.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Let me ask you this -- if we could please go to tab 98, to 65 ter number 6604. If we could go to page -- towards page 3, please. And the subject line for that is: International search for perpetrators of criminal acts.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. I didn't see this. I saw Interpol's red notice. That's what I saw. But I've never seen that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And on -- on the second page -- sorry, the -- the next page after this one, and it describes the allegations regarding the ill-treatment of detainees at the end by Ilija Celar; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see what it says, but I don't think it's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You don't think it's true?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we go to the second page of this document, it describes Ilija Celar as a member of a special police unit, that he arrested the non-Serb population of Baranja, brought them to the prison and beat them. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you say all of the charges were resolved in 2006.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in 2011, Interpol wrote to us saying they were withdrawing the red -- because they had nothing against him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could we go to the last page of this document. And I believe the -- the page in B/C/S would be 105 in e-court page numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, if we could just enlarge that a little bit, you can see that this has Ilija Celar's name and his signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Is that his signature?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would say yes, the one on the left is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, what says is "To Attorney Branko Nenadic from Darda, so he may represent me in the criminal case before the county court in Osijek on the basis of a decision of 3 August 2009 concerning suspended criminal proceedings raised against me ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: "And to submit this proposal and undertake all work according to the Law on Criminal Procedure in order to obtain a withdrawal of the international arrest warrant against Ilija Celar." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And do you see the date at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So I'm a bit confused about you saying, on the one hand, that all the charges were dismissed in 2006, and here is Ilija Celar asking for the withdrawal of the international arrest warrant --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's what we did it for because we had to -- in order to get the withdrawal of the Interpol, we had to -- he had to prove that that warrant was no longer outstanding, and that's why he employed the lawyer to go and find out what was happening with the Osijek court. And that's where I understood that they'd come to there -- that 9 -- 16 of them were published outside the court. I thought it was 2006 because we were a bit cross that nobody ever told us, that nobody went to Osijek and -- it wasn't in a newspaper. It was stuck on the building outside the court, the decision of the court was made then.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And it's based on that, you say, why this letter is being written by Ilija Celar?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because it was around 2011 that we started writing asking -- once we'd found out about the decision of 2006, we began writing to Interpol, asking them why this red notice was still in evidence, and then it took -- I don't know how long it took but it took a long time for their decision to come through, and he's got the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If you would be so kind, we would like a copy of that.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I must tell you, Mrs. Celar, that the Prosecution believes that, in fact, based on the information given, that Ilija Celar did participate in the maltreatment of detainees at the Beli Manastir police station.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is totally in opposition. I know some did, but he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Other people did, but he did not?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was one of a few that didn't. And it took courage not to, to go and protect -- it was not a particularly popular thing to do but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Why wasn't it popular?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there were some criminals doing things, like stealing things and he would try and intervene. I'm not talking about ill-treatment by -- in the jail. I'm talking about the criminal element that were taking houses and everything and he -- cars. He tried to stop that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: But I am talking about killings and beatings --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- torture?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe that my husband would be involved in killings, beatings and torture. Categorically not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Before we eventually move to something else in that -- the document that is on the screen now, reference is made to -- and it's the basis of the document, the document says, "a decision of 3 August 2009 concerning suspended criminal proceedings raised against me ..." Do you have that 3 August 2009 decision, and do you know what is referred to by "suspended criminal proceedings"?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll have to -- it's a very voluminous document and I believe the document is contained in it. It hasn't been translated, if it is there, and I would like to verify, again, my belief it is there before I say categorically that it is. My understanding, which may be imperfect, is that by "suspension" what they meant was as the accused were not available as they had left the -- Croatia, the proceedings were suspended in time. But that is my understanding after a very quick review of the documents that we got in. And in that regard, frankly, I will continue with the cross-examination of Mrs. Celar, but it may be that we have -- after review of them, we may need more time -- we may have more questions for Mrs. Celar at a later stage, if the Court understands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, Madam Celar, you previously described how Serbs were dismissed from their jobs.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you -- in Osijek.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you also described how the names of certain streets were changed.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In Osijek, I believe.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know where?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They weren't all in Osijek. Some of them were in Zagreb, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And do I understand you correctly that the dismissals and the change in the names and all of that gave you the sense that things were becoming increasingly hostile?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: For Serbs?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Are you aware of the measures taken by the authorities in Baranja regarding employment, THE right of return --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- and the change of names? I'd like to take a look at 2157. P, excuse me. Which is tab 29. And, first, I'd like to go to the last page. And do you see that this is signed by Borivoje Zivanovic? Do you see the name in the lower --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, this is right after the take-over of Beli Manastir and in the Baranja area generally. And do you see it is entitled "On termination of employment and prohibition to return and stay in Baranja, all persons who were in the enemy forces and people who helped them and their immediate families." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And in the first article, --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, it's in Serbian. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In the first article, you see that: "The decision regulates the issue of employment termination and prohibition to return and stay in Baranja ... all persons who were in enemy units on the Baranja territory, to their collaborators as well as to their immediate family members."

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So would you agree that that appears to relate to the termination of employment for family members of people suspected to be --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- in enemy units? Were you aware that such restrictions had been put on family members?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because I only knew -- all the people I mention in Osijek, I knew them personally and they came to see us. But I don't know -- I've never seen that. I wasn't aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we could move to the next tab, P30, which is tab 30, P2158.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I continued, I wondered if I could have an indication of how much time I've used so far. Just a technical time-keeping issue, Mrs. Celar, if you could just bear with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] two and a half hours, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And, again, this is around 24 September 1991 and it's a decision, again, on the termination of employment for all persons who openly supported the overthrown regime of the Republic of Croatia. And do you see at the bottom, Mr. Borivoje Zivanovic's name?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you know about this decision?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And I'll direct your attention to the first article: "This decision regulates the termination of employment of all persons who openly supported the overthrown regime of the Republic of Croatia and who, if they remain at their place of employment, would disturb the formal work process or irritate other employees, which could lead to serious, specific and political problems, regardless of their ethnic or religious affiliations." So did you know that people were targeted based on the perception of whether or not they supported the overthrown regime?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't there then, again, and I think when I was there he wasn't president, he was mayor.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So you didn't know about this type of legislation?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because if I had, I would have -- I did have a meeting with him, Borivoje Zivanovic, about attacks on Croats and asked him to go on the radio and ask people not to do it because surely they didn't want to behave the way the Croatians behaved in Osijek, and surely they would not want the world to see Serbia in that light.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And did he often go on Radio Beli Manastir?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Is that the radio station [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I didn't have a meeting with him at the radio station.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Where was he?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to his office and asked him if he would and he said it wasn't possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Had you asked him to go on the radio -- and which radio is that? I'm assuming it's --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been the local radio.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Beli Manastir --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't specific. I said could he make an appeal that people could -- the fighting was over at that point. Could they -- or I'm not sure it was over or not, but could he please appeal to people's decency not to attack. It was at the time of the Ratkajec family, and I was deeply disturbed by their unhappiness, and I went there with Ilija to ask him to make an appeal.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Which radio station did you have in mind that he would make the appeal on?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't think about it. I would have supposed it would be Baranja, the one in Beli Manastir.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Had you heard him on the radio before?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't listen to the radio.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be -- I know it's a little bit earlier but this would be a good time for me before I start the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Biersay. We take our first break. Thirty minutes. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I know the witness is being brought in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It's okay. It's actually good because I wanted to give the e-court pages for the B/C/S document that you asked about in the files relating to Ilija Celar. And specifically they're e-court pages 109 to 113, but my understanding is that the Defence may be addressing it later anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Biersay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to now show you Exhibit P2159, which is tab 31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That seems to be under seal, Ms. Biersay; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. So not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If we could go to the third page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did -- thank you. Did -- did you hear about people being given notice through the media that they had to leave --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- the area? I'd like to direct your attention to this document, which is attached to a decision to terminate employment and what the decision states is: "We hereby notify you that you must leave the area of Baranja within 24 hours because you were involved in some way with the HDZ and assisted the Ustasha authorities. All those who were involved in any way have been informed through the media that they must leave." "In order for everyone to be aware that this relates to you or your family, go in full view of everyone so that you do not end up dead. "Good-bye, Ustasha." Mrs. Celar, I wondered in reading this, is this the kind of document -- decision that would encourage someone to stay?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's horrible.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we could now turn to Exhibit P2160, which is exhibit -- excuse me, it's tab 32. And if we could go to the third page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: While that's coming up on the screen, Mrs. Celar, you talked about how you, with the right paperwork, could come and go to Baranja?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly come and go. I had to go and ask for an exit and then when I returned, ask for an entry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Were you ever refused entry?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention to this decision. And at the bottom, you'll see that it has been signed by President Borivoje Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at the top, there he's listed as president and you'll see at the top, it says: "At the fourth session held on 18 October 1991, the Executive Council of Beli Manastir," and it describes them adopting this decision. And this decision is to ban from returning all persons who failed to return to Beli Manastir municipality by 25 September 1991. Article 1 reads that: "All persons, regardless of their ethnicity and religion, who failed to return to the area of Beli Manastir municipality by 25 September 1991 ..." And at the end: "... shall be banned from returning." So were you aware that persons who had not returned to the municipality by that date --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because a lot of them came back later and they were Serbs who'd gone while the fighting was going on. I know several people who didn't come back until later or even the next year.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when say "several people" you mean Serb fighters?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I mean Serbs who weren't fighters. A Serbian lawyer friend of ours, he didn't come back until, oh, it was December or maybe later. And a lot of the families that went to Prigrevica. I don't think they came back within that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's others as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It's our position, the Prosecution's position, that that was especially targeting non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know of others that came back. In fact, my brother-in-law came back and he was Croat.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when did he come back?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this year, because he was there all the time. And then he left to go and visit - I can't remember the date - he went to visit his mother in Zagreb because they were ill. Then he was arrested in Croatia and then he came back into Serbia, but I don't know the year. It's -- I wrote about it to a newspaper, but, I'm sorry, I just can't recall the date. But he was -- that's one I knew about that wasn't a Serb. They came from Hungary, not Batina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if you compare the ones that you knew about, the Serbs versus non-Serbs, would you say more Serbs came back?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say because I didn't know that many of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You didn't know --

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that many Serbs but I don't -- I wasn't aware that a lot of them had even left. When I met them in the town, I didn't know they'd been somewhere else so -- unless they told me. So I can't really give a -- an opinion on that with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to now turn your attention to P -- Exhibit P2161, which is tab 33. And while it's coming up, I'll tell you this is a decision by the Executive Council of Beli Manastir, and the purpose of decision is to change the street names in the town of Beli Manastir. Were you aware that the names of the streets changed by decision of the Executive Council?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice. I've seen this list since, and some of them are Communist names or celebrating victories of Tito, et cetera. They're not all people. But I wasn't aware of it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if I could direct your attention on the first page, for example, to 14, 15, and 16, the Vojvoda's names?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Vladimir Lenin. That's Lenin's name, 15, and I think they mean Vladimir Ilic Lenin, the Russian.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: That's in the current street name column. If you go ...

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see, to the opposite. I was looking at the wrong one, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: To the opposite -- yes.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes. Yes, Dukes they changed it to. From Dukes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And Dukes are associated with what period of time of Serbian history; do you know?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Vojvoda wasn't exactly a duke. I think it was something awarded for bravery in battle. It could date back to Kosovo, I suppose. I'm not sure. We translate it as "dukes," but it's sort of a honorary title.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at the time -- you said you've seen this list since. Did you know about the change of the street names at the time that it occurred?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now in your statement, in paragraph 53 - and I think you were also asked about this on direct - you talked about the desire of Serb refugees to come to Baranja, and you reference that it may have -- "their desire may have been a result of family relations or desire to stay as close as possible to the places from which they had fled." Do you see?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Are you aware that various people associated with the Serbian authorities in Baranja invited Serb refugees to come to Baranja?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not -- I didn't notice that. I wasn't aware that there were invitations being sent out. I just thought they came because they'd got nowhere else to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And I'd like to turn to Exhibit P165, tab 5. And I believe the -- this document is dated around the fall of Vukovar from November 1991. Let me ask you this while this is being prepared. Have you heard of Rade Leskovac?

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I see that written?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: AMANDA CELAR [Resumed]
